advisories.title: Domoticz is a free, open source home automation system for Linux, Windows, macOS, and Raspberry Pi
advisories.summary: Domoticz is a free, open source home automation system for Linux, Windows, macOS, and Raspberry Pi. Prior to 2026.3, the `udevices` JSON command handler, `Cmd_UpdateDevices` in `main/WebServerCmds.cpp`, performed no `session.rights` check before invoking a Lua parser script, while its sibling command handlers gate access by role. A low-privilege authenticated user could trigger execution of an existing operator-installed Lua parser script with attacker-controlled input through the `GET /json.htm` endpoint with `type=command` and `param=udevices`. The `script` parameter also lacked a `..` path-traversal guard: `CLuaHandler::executeLuaScript` in `main/LuaHandler.cpp` constructed the filename from the parser directory and the supplied script name before passing it to `luaL_loadfile`. Execution is limited to already-installed valid Lua files; this is not arbitrary code execution, and the advisory states that file-write and upload paths require administrator privileges. This issue is addressed in version 2026.3.

advisories.summary: Asterisk is an open source private branch exchange and telephony toolkit. advisories.summary: ### Summary On MLflow tracking servers running without authentication, which is the default for mlflow server, a remote attacker can read arbitrary files from the server’s filesystem by creating a model version tagged as a prompt whose source is a schemeless local path. Servers using `--app-name basic-auth` are also affected: any authenticated user can create a registered model, so a low-privilege account can use this to read the authentication database, including the admin password hash. advisories.title: undici vulnerable to cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure via cross-origin redirects
advisories.summary: ### Impact When an originless `Agent` composes the redirect and cache interceptors as `compose(redirect(), cache())` with a shared cache (`type: 'shared'`), the cache builds its key from the original request URL before the redirect handler changes the origin. The response produced after a redirect is then stored under the original key, even when the redirect crossed to a different origin. An attacker who controls the target of a redirect from a trusted URL can have their response cached under that trusted URL. A later caller requesting the trusted URL receives the attacker's body from the shared cache without either origin being contacted, allowing persistent cache poisoning. advisories.title: undici vulnerable to Denial of Service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation
advisories.summary: ## Impact undici crashes the client process when a TLS 1.2 server renegotiates after the connection is established and presents a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname does not match the requested host. advisories.title: undici WebSocket client vulnerable to Denial of Service via unbounded automatic PONG buffering
advisories.summary: ### Impact undici's WebSocket client (including Node.js's bundled `globalThis.WebSocket`) can be driven to exhaust process memory by a malicious or compromised WebSocket server. For every PING frame received, the receiver automatically writes a PONG response to the socket and ignores the `false` return value from `socket.write()`, which is a backpressure signal, so a server that streams small PING frames while never reading the client's PONGs makes the outbound write queue and heap grow without bound until the Node.js process runs out of memory and terminates. The attack is remote and unauthenticated, needs only a normal WebSocket connection, and is asymmetric: small inbound PINGs produce a much larger retained outbound queue. Availability is the only impact. undici 5.x, 6.x, 7.x, and 8.x are affected; the WebSocket client was introduced in 5.15.0. ### Patches Upgrade to `6.29.1`, `7.30.1`, or `8.12.2`, which pause WebSocket frame parsing when the automatic PONG response hits socket backpressure and resume on drain, bounding the outbound queue. ### Workarounds None.

advisories.title: Symfony: Unbounded Recursion in the YAML Inline Lexer Lets a Single Document Crash the Process
advisories.summary: ### Description `Yaml\Parser::lexInlineStructure()` recursed through `lexInlineMapping()` and `lexInlineSequence()` for every `{` and `[` of an inline collection, without entering the nesting level that the rest of the parser bounds with `maxNestingLevel`. advisories.title: Authlib accepts an empty HMAC key, allowing JWS/JWT signature forgery (HS256/HS384/HS512)

Summary Authlib's symmetric (oct) key handling accepts an empty key (empty bytes b'' / empty string '') as a valid HMAC signing and verification key. An empty HMAC key produces a deterministic digest that any party can reproduce, so an attacker who knows (or can cause) the application to verify a token with an empty key can forge arbitrary tokens that pass HS256/HS384/HS512 signature verification. This is the Authlib member of the cross-language empty-HMAC-key family already assigned CVE-2026-44351 (fast-jwt, npm) and CVE-2026-45363 (ruby-jwt, RubyGems). This is DISTINCT from Authlib's existing recent JWT-verification advisories. It is not closed by CVE-2026-27962 / GHSA-wvwj-cvrp-7pv5 (JWS JWK header injection, the key=None case), nor by CVE-2026-28802 / GHSA-7wc2-qxgw-g8gg (alg:none blank-signature bypass), nor by GHSA-5357-c2jx-v7qh (algorithm confusion with asymmetric public keys). Those address header-driven key injection, the none algorithm, and asymmetric-vs-symmetric confusion respectively; none of them rejects a zero-length oct key. advisories.title: Authlib incomplete algorithm-confusion fix permits HMAC forgery with prefixed public keys
advisories.summary: ## Summary `OctKey.import_key()` carries the only guard that stops an asymmetric public key from being used as an HMAC secret in `authlib.jose`. That guard is `raw_key.startswith(POSSIBLE_UNSAFE_KEYS)` — anchored at byte 0 — while the loader that consumes the identical bytes on the asymmetric path (`cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization.load_pem_public_key` / `load_pem_x509_certificate`) skips anything before the `-----BEGIN` line. A PEM public key or X.509 certificate carrying **one leading byte** — a newline, a space, four spaces of indentation, a UTF-8 BOM, or a comment line — is therefore not recognised, falls through, and becomes the HMAC secret. An attacker holding only the issuer's public key then mints an `HS256` token with arbitrary claims that `jwt.decode()` accepts as authentic. This is an incomplete fix of **CVE-2024-37568 / GHSA-5357-c2jx-v7qh**. That advisory's fix is exactly this guard (`git log -S 'POSSIBLE_UNSAFE_KEYS' -- authlib/jose/rfc7518/oct_key.py` returns a single commit, `3bea812` "fix: prevent OctKey to import ssh/rsa/pem keys", referencing issue #654), and the original attack works again unchanged whenever the stored PEM does not start at offset 0. Reproduced end-to-end on **1.8.0**, the newest release (published 2026-08-30), and on `origin/main`

advisories.title: PhpSpreadsheet: XmlScanner Bypass via ISO-2022 Escape Sequences Allows XXE and Denial of Service
advisories.summary: ### Summary PhpSpreadsheet's `XmlScanner::scan()` uses a regex pattern that only accounts for NULL byte (0x00) interleaving when detecting `<!DOCTYPE`. ISO-2022 escape sequences (0x1B bytes) inserted between the characters of the pattern break the regex match entirely, allowing DOCTYPE declarations with entity definitions to pass through undetected. This enables Denial of Service via quadratic entity expansion on **all PHP versions**, and XXE/SSRF on PHP < 8.0 or when `LIBXML_NOENT` is used. Any application using PhpSpreadsheet to process user-uploaded XLSX files is affected. ### Details The vulnerability exists in `src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Security/XmlScanner.php`, method `scan()`, lines 87–100. The scanner builds a regex pattern `/\0*<\0*!\0*D\0*O\0*C\0*T\0*Y\0*P\0*E\0*/` that only handles NULL byte interleaving. ISO-2022 escape sequences (e.g., `0x1B 0x28 0x42` for ISO-2022-JP) inserted between each character of `<!DOCTYPE` break the regex because it only expects optional `\0` between characters. The XLSX reader extracts XML parts from the ZIP archive and passes each through `XmlScanner::scan()` before `simplexml_load_string()`. advisories.title: Datadog dd-trace-py: ReDoS in URL query string obfuscation
advisories.summary: ### Summary A regular expression used to obfuscate URL query strings can consume excessive CPU when processing certain attacker-controlled input. advisories.title: MongoDB Python Driver: Out-of-bounds read in BSON decoding via a malformed Regex element
advisories.summary: ### Impact The C extension's BSON decoder scans a Regex element's pattern and flags strings with strlen before checking the document's remaining length, so a crafted truncated Regex element can read past the end of the caller's buffer. bson.decode and bson.decode_all accept mmap and array buffers, which carry no NUL sentinel; the read can cross into unmapped memory and kill the process with an uncatchable SIGSEGV. Any application decoding untrusted BSON from such buffers is affected — impact is availability only, since the out-of-bounds bytes are never returned as content. NUL-terminated buffers (bytes, bytearray) raise `InvalidBSON` at worst; the driver's own transport and pure-Python installs are not affected. All releases through 4.18.2 are affected when the C extension is loaded. ### Patches Fixed in PyMongo 4.18.3. Malformed Regex elements now raise InvalidBSON on every accepted buffer type; valid documents decode unchanged. ### Workarounds Decode untrusted BSON only from NUL-terminated buffers — bytes or bytearray — and copy mmap input first, e.g. bytes(mm[:size]).
advisories.remediation: pymongo: 4.18.3

advisories.summary: There is a local confidentiality issue in the default `FileSessionManager` storage behavior. By default it writes session data under `/tmp/strands/sessions` and relies on the process umask for directory and file permissions. advisories.title: Flexible GraphRAG: Cypher/Graph Injection via broken string-escaping in FalkorDB adapter (_escape()) - full graph wipe from ingested-document content
advisories.summary: **Description** def _escape(v: str) -> str: return str(v).replace("'", "\\'").replace("\\", "\\\\") The escaping order is backwards, exactly like the classic HTML double-escape bug: step 1 inserts a literal backslash in front of every ', then step 2 re-matches that just-inserted backslash and doubles it. For an input ending in a single quote, the two steps combined produce \\' (two backslashes followed by the quote) in the output — which, under the standard backslash-escape convention used by Cypher/openCypher single-quoted string literals, is parsed as one escaped backslash followed by an unescaped, string-terminating quote. The quote is not neutralized; the string breaks open. advisories.title: LiteLLM: internal_user_viewer arbitrary local file read via `vertex_ai_credentials`
advisories.summary: ## Summary An authenticated LiteLLM proxy user could read arbitrary local files from the proxy runtime by sending a crafted `vertex_ai_credentials` value to `/utils/transform_request`. advisories.title: GitPython: Submodule.move() follows an attacker-committed intermediate symlink outside the worktree
advisories.summary: ## Summary GitPython's public `Submodule.move()` API verifies that its destination is lexically inside the parent repository, but it does not reject symbolic links in the destination's intermediate components before filesystem operations. advisories.title: Agno: Arbitrary code execution via `eval()` on `field_type` in `FunctionCall`
advisories.summary: ### Impact Agno versions prior to 2.3.24 contain an arbitrary code execution vulnerability in the model execution component. The `field_type` parameter on a `FunctionCall` input field was passed to Python's built-in `eval()`, allowing an attacker who could influence that value to execute arbitrary Python code in the Agno process. The unsafe `eval()` call was replaced with a fixed `type_mapping` dictionary lookup, and `field_type` is now validated as either a known string key or an already-resolved `type` object before use. The current release line (2.6.x) includes the fix. ### Workarounds There is no safe workaround. advisories.summary: ### Summary A SQL Injection vulnerability exists in the Third Party (Company) update functionality of Dolibarr ERP/CRM. advisories.summary: ### Summary `authlib.common.security.is_secure_transport()` is used throughout Authlib to enforce the OAuth 2.0 / OIDC requirement that endpoint and redirect URIs use TLS, with an RFC 8252 §7.3 exemption for loopback `http://` URIs. The check is implemented as a textual `str.startswith` prefix match, so a URL such as `http://localhost:80@evil.example/cb` — whose actual host is `evil.example` and whose scheme is plain `http` — is accepted as "secure". advisories.title: @better-auth/drizzle-adapter: Concurrent requests can exceed rate limits on PostgreSQL
advisories.summary: ## Am I affected? You are affected if you use `@better-auth/drizzle-adapter` from 1.6.17 through versions before 1.7.7 (including the 1.7.0 prereleases from beta.6 through rc.6) or `@better-auth/kysely-adapter` 1.6.17 through 1.6.31, and keep rate-limit records in a PostgreSQL database. All of these must be true: - Rate limiting is enabled. - Rate-limit records are stored in the database. - The database is PostgreSQL, used through one of the adapter versions above. You are not affected if you store rate-limit records in memory (the default) or in secondary storage. ## Summary Database-backed rate limiting on PostgreSQL can let a burst of concurrent requests go over the configured maximum. When many requests arrive at the same time, several of them can pass the limit check together. This weakens the rate limit on password sign-in, two-factor verification, one-time codes, password resets, and other rate-limited endpoints. ## Impact An attacker who sends many requests at once can make more attempts than the application allows. The issue does not bypass password or one-time-code validation. It does not directly compromise an account. The number of extra attempts is limited by the number of concurrent database connections, the number of application instances, and the rate-limit window

advisories.title: Twisted: DNS Response Spoofing in twisted.names Due to Missing Source Address Validation
advisories.summary: ### Summary `twisted.names.dns.DNSDatagramProtocol`, the UDP transport used by twisted's DNS client (`twisted.names.client.Resolver`, `createResolver`, and anything built on it, including MX lookups in `twisted.mail`), accepts a DNS response for a pending query solely on the basis of the 16-bit transaction ID matching. It never checks that the response actually originated from the server the query was sent to. Any host that can deliver a UDP packet to the resolver's listening port with the correct transaction ID can inject a forged answer, independent of the real server's address. This is a materially weaker defense than standard DNS resolver practice (transaction ID plus source-address validation, typically also source-port rotation), and enables off-path DNS response spoofing / cache poisoning. ### Details `DNSDatagramProtocol.datagramReceived` (`src/twisted/names/dns.py`, line 3350) is: ```python def datagramReceived(self, data, addr): """ Read a datagram, extract the message in it and trigger the associated Deferred. advisories.title: Malicious code in publish-poc-test3 (npm)
advisories.summary: ## Source: amazon-inspector (4001a75b24abfa181a10e5d40931194f254304fcf5fda554488d3c242cc5db85) The package's postinstall lifecycle script creates a temporary directory, writes a fabricated package.json whose name is 'publish-poc-found-<random-hex>' (random suffix derived via 'openssl rand -hex 2'), and then invokes 'npm publish' from that directory. The literal string 'npm publish' is reconstructed at runtime by concatenating three fragments ('np', 'm pu', 'blish') through printf, specifically to prevent manifest and string scanners from matching the command. The publish runs against the public npm registry using whatever npm authentication context the installing environment currently has (an _authToken from ~/.npmrc, NPM_TOKEN / NODE_AUTH_TOKEN in the environment, or an active CI publish identity), so running 'npm install' of this package on a developer workstation or CI host that holds publish rights causes a new attacker-named package to be published under the installer's npm identity. The combination of credential abuse at install time, randomized attacker-chosen package naming, and deliberate obfuscation of the exact command performing the publish is characteristic registry self-propagation / worm behavior. --- Credit: [OpenSSF](https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages) ([

advisories.summary: dsh-plugin-blender-3d@0.2.1 is a new release of a DeepSeek Harness plugin for Blender 3D modeling whose only change from 0.2.0 is a postinstall script, `sh scripts/miner.sh`, that runs on npm install. The script downloads a gzip carrier from amplify-gursha-dev-121835-deployment.s3.amazonaws.com to /tmp/.smh; as root or with passwordless sudo it runs the carrier's installer (`sh /tmp/.smi agent`), which installs an XMRig miner plus two helper daemons under random system-component names and persists them as systemd units or @reboot cron entries, and otherwise it extracts the bundled XMRig binary to ~/.local/lib/<random name>/ and mines Monero to networkservicesupp.flashhub.net:8443 over TLS with a hardcoded wallet. advisories.title: Malicious code in @sxm-web/client-sdk-core (npm)
advisories.summary: @sxm-web/client-sdk-core is a dependency-confusion package: it is described as a "Compatibility shim", uses inflated version numbers, and its README calls it an "authorized dependency-confusion test". Each listed version (0.0.1, 1.0.0, 1.0.1, 2.0.0, 1.1.0, 3.0.0, 13.3.7) has a postinstall script that runs `node beacon.cjs` on npm install, and index.js calls the same code when the package is imported; it POSTs the hostname, install path and current working directory over plain HTTP to `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`, and index.js exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions so builds importing the real package keep running. The npm account wiseke published 14 such packages under the @greenlake, @sxm-web, @drone-js-ext and @ppa-web-components scopes between 2026-10-23 21:23 and 2026-10-25 14:28 UTC; index.js is byte-identical to that of ph-common (MAL-2026-1809), which sends to the same endpoint. --- Credit: [OpenSSF](https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages) ([source](https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages/blob/38576efe4884e97a0598f23da7c6da0343b22df4/osv/malicious/npm/@sxm-web/client-sdk-core/MAL-2026-18319.json))

advisories.title: A vulnerability has been identified in BRAIN2 versions up to and including version 3.09
advisories.summary: A vulnerability has been identified in BRAIN2 versions up to and including version 3.09. Under specific installation conditions, the password of a Windows service account may be written in cleartext to a setup log file. The issue occurs when Microsoft SQL Server access is configured using Integrated Security and the Windows account intended to run the BRAIN2 MainService is specified during execution of the BRAIN2 installation wizard. The setup log file is stored in the temporary directory of the Windows administrator performing the installation. This directory is not accessible to standard Windows users and can generally only be accessed by users with administrative privileges. Successful exploitation could result in the disclosure of credentials belonging to the configured BRAIN2 service account.

advisories.title: An insecure deserialization (PHP object injection) vulnerability exists in Mautic's handling of segment filters and custom field properties
advisories.summary: An insecure deserialization (PHP object injection) vulnerability exists in Mautic's handling of segment filters and custom field properties. Several code paths that read these stored values from the database deserialize them without restricting which PHP classes may be instantiated, instead of using Mautic's safe deserialization helper. An attacker who is able to store a crafted serialized value in these segment filter or custom field properties can cause arbitrary PHP objects to be instantiated when Mautic later processes the data, for example during segment evaluation, contact export, or custom field API requests. Combined with gadget chains available in Mautic's dependencies, this could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server, read, modify, or delete data stored in the Mautic instance, including contact data, and affect its availability. Exploitation requires high privileges or an existing ability to write to the affected stored data.

advisories.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/vc4: drain the hangcheck timer and works on V3D unbind Nothing stops the hangcheck timer that submitted jobs arm, or the job_done_work that the render-done interrupt queues, at teardown: vc4_irq_disable() cancels only overflow_mem_work, and vc4_gem_destroy() runs from the drm-managed release, after vc4_v3d_unbind() has already uninstalled the V3D interrupt and cleared vc4->v3d. A timer still armed by then reads V3D registers through the NULL vc4->v3d pointer, and the late callbacks run on the vc4_dev embedding them after it has been freed. Drain them in vc4_v3d_unbind(): shut the timer down and cancel reset_work before the interrupt is taken down, because its vc4_irq_reset() re-enables it, then flush job_done_work so that completions queued at teardown still release their jobs. This issue was found by an in-house static analysis tool.

advisories.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/register: don't exempt disabled rings from task restrictions A ring created with IORING_SETUP_R_DI
advisories.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/register: don't exempt disabled rings from task restrictions A ring created with IORING_SETUP_R_DISABLED is exempt from its register restrictions until it is enabled. This lets the creator register the restrictions and then enable the ring with IORING_REGISTER_ENABLE_RINGS, whether or not that opcode is in the allowed set. Since commit ed82f35b926b ("io_uring: allow registration of per-task restrictions"), a ring also inherits restrictions from the task that creates it, and the same exemption applies to those. A task whose register opcodes are restricted can therefore create a disabled ring, issue any register opcode on it, and then enable it. Mark rings whose restrictions were inherited from the task, and keep checking register opcodes for them while the ring is disabled. Enabling such a ring now requires IORING_REGISTER_ENABLE_RINGS to be in the task's allowed set. Per-ring restrictions registered on a disabled ring work as before. [axboe: amend with inheritance flag fixup]

advisories.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: dm-integrity: fix buffer overflow in inline mode with large tag size In inline mode, dm_integrity_check and
advisories.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: dm-integrity: fix buffer overflow in inline mode with large tag size In inline mode, dm_integrity_check and dm_integrity_inline_recheck compute the checksum of each block into an on-stack buffer of HASH_MAX_DIGESTSIZE bytes. integrity_sector_checksum pads its result with zeroes up to the tag size, so if the tag size is larger than HASH_MAX_DIGESTSIZE, the padding runs past the end of the buffer. With CONFIG_STACKPROTECTOR the kernel panics in dm_integrity_check on the first read. Enlarge both buffers to hold MAX_TAG_SIZE bytes, as commit b93b6643e9b5 ("dm integrity: fix a crash with unusually large tag size") did for integrity_metadata. Note that this is not a security bug because the buffer overflow can only be triggered by root.

advisories.summary: Burrito is a Terraform Automation Collaboration Software (TACoS) Kubernetes operator. Anyone who can reach `burrito-server`'s endpoint and knows a tracked repository's URL can forge events to create or delete `TerraformPullRequest` custom resources with attacker-chosen `Branch`, `Base`, and `ID` fields. For GitHub `pull_request` events, the controller fetches changed files using the real pull request number but does not cross-check the payload's branch against that pull request. Pairing a real, existing pull request number with an unrelated existing branch in the same repository can therefore cause an unauthorized `terraform plan` for affected layers using the operator's stored git and cloud credentials. advisories.title: .NET Brotli decompression out of bounds write
advisories.summary: An out of bounds memory write in the Brotli decoder used by modern .NET and ASP.NET Core may cause memory corruption, information disclosure, denial of service or privilege elevation when the application decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data. Automatic request/response decompression is disabled by default. On Windows, PHP 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 and 8.2.35-1 package rebuilds include Brotli 1.2.1 to fix this vulnerability in cURL decompression dependencies; it is not an additional PHP language CVE.
advisories.affected: Affected .NET 8 versions earlier than 8.0.33, .NET 9 earlier than 9.0.22, .NET 10 earlier than 10.0.14, and affected .NET 11 prereleases earlier than RC3. Specific NativeAOT and runtime packs vary by platform. Classic .NET Framework is not affected by this CVE. PHP Windows builds without the October 26 -1 Brotli dependency rebuild may carry a vulnerable decoder in the cURL extension when automatic HTTP decompression is enabled.
advisories.remediation: Update affected installations to .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22 or 10.0.14 (or .NET 11 RC3 for prerelease installations). Rebuild self-contained apps and containers with the fixed runtimes, and update affected NuGet packages where the advisory requires it. For affected PHP Windows distributions, install the corresponding PHP 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 or 8.2.35-1 build including Brotli 1.2.1.
advisories.exploitation: Confirmed: listed in CISA KEV
advisories.status: Vendor-sourced historical baseline; not newly disclosed

advisories.title: Malicious code in event-bus-lite-testmetest (npm)
advisories.summary: ## Source: amazon-inspector (038b62e6040cef7e651f3cf89c146290f391c28977fe206410408e85ccbe4721) The package ships a binding.gyp whose target has type "none" and no C/C++ source files; its only purpose is a GYP `<!(...)` command-expansion that runs `node index.js` during the automatic `node-gyp rebuild` triggered by `npm install`. index.js is multi-layer obfuscated: a char-code array is Caesar-decoded (shift 21) and passed to eval; the decoded body reads the bundled lib_native.dat (~312 KB, high-entropy, sha256 e1ab1e330d3db532d511d4af4386ab2d2c6245ca807410f51c1211ae48814d73), brotli-decompresses and AES-128-GCM-decrypts it with hardcoded key/IV/AAD, writes the plaintext to a `mkdtempSync('.b-')/index.js` temp path, and spawns the Bun runtime (`Bun.spawn`, or `getBunPath()` via child_process.spawn) to execute the decrypted payload. Executing under Bun bypasses Node-only analysis. The contents of the executed payload are not inspectable from the shipped artifact. --- Credit: [OpenSSF](https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages) ([source](https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages/blob/01084f0336ff5489308aeadf45facfcb3ceab9ec/osv/malicious/npm/event-bus-lite-testmetest/MAL-2026-18292.json))

advisories.title: DSA-6584-1 varnish - security update
advisories.summary:
Several vulnerabilities were discovered in Varnish Cache, an HTTP accelerator, which could result in cache poisoning, authentication bypass or denial of service.

CVE-2026-34475

Tom Kinnaird discovered a deficiency in the parsing of HTTP/1.1 absolute-form request targets. If the request URL is passed unchecked to a backend which accepts absolute-form URIs, a remote attacker could potentially poison the cache or bypass authentication. The issue affects requests for root URLs.

CVE-2026-93894

Tristan Madani discovered a workspace buffer overflow in the .upper() and .lower() string methods of the Varnish Configuration Language. A remote attacker with knowledge of the active configuration could craft a request which exhausts the remaining workspace during case conversion, causing the worker process to crash and restart, resulting in denial of service. Exploitation depends on the configuration using these methods on attacker-controlled strings and on the applicable request size limits.

https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/DSA-6584-1

advisories.title: PHP session upload progress security advisory under unusual configuration
advisories.summary: The PHP project identified an additional potential remote code execution vector involving session upload progress and an unusual sequence: an application configures session.serialize_handler as php_binary or php_serialize, switches it to php at runtime using ini_set, and then calls session_start. This specific issue was not fixed by the October 21 security releases. Vendor rates the circumstance unlikely; no standalone CVSS rating is asserted here.
advisories.affected: PHP installations that enable session.upload_progress and use the unusual runtime session.serialize_handler switching sequence. Affected version ranges and the precise final fixed version await the PHP project's dedicated advisory.
advisories.remediation: Until the dedicated patch is available, set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 in the administrative PHP configuration and restart relevant PHP workers if the feature is not required. Review application behavior. Follow future upstream PHP advisories for the actual fix.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed active exploitation of this separate configuration-dependent issue in the cited PHP announcement.
advisories.status: Vendor-sourced historical baseline; not newly disclosed
advisories.action: Verify the affected version and exposure, then follow the vendor remediation.

advisories.title: filelock: ReadWriteLock on the hard-link route deletes any directory another user renames onto its .filelock-* link directory name
advisories.summary: `ReadWriteLock` and `AsyncReadWriteLock` (the SQLite-backed reader/writer lock) remove their private `.filelock-*` link directories with `shutil.rmtree` (a recursive delete) on a remembered path. They do not check that the path still names the directory they created. This happens on the hard-link route (a hard link is a second name for the same file). That route is every connection on macOS since 4.1.1 and any POSIX process without a usable `/proc/self/fd` (a Linux path that names the process's own open files), such as a chroot or container that does not mount `/proc`. Another local user who can rename entries in the directory that holds the lock database can rename one of the directories of the user running the lock (below: the lock user) onto the link directory's name, or onto a forged dead-holder name. Such a lock directory is a `0777` or group-writable cache, build or project directory without the sticky bit (a directory flag that lets only a file's owner remove or rename it). The lock user's process then deletes that tree and everything in it with the lock user's permissions, and reports no error. Stock Linux with `/proc` mounted is not affected. Affected versions are filelock 4.1.0 through 4.2.0. Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this in private as `ANT-2026-LSSZIUEO` [high,

advisories.title: filelock: ReadWriteLock on Windows acts on SQLite side files another local user places beside its database
advisories.summary: On Windows, `ReadWriteLock` and `AsyncReadWriteLock` (the SQLite-backed reader/writer lock) connect SQLite to the lock database by its path, in every directory. SQLite derives three side files from that path: `<database>-journal`, the rollback journal (pages saved to undo an interrupted write); `<database>-wal`, the write-ahead log (changes kept outside the main file); and `<database>-shm`, the shared-memory index of the WAL. SQLite acts on whichever of these it finds beside the database before the lock runs any statement. Another local account that can create files in the database's directory, but not delete files of other accounts there, places such a side file beside the database and denies everyone `DELETE` on it, which a file's creator may do. `C:\Windows\Temp` (the temporary directory of services, granting `BUILTIN\Users` create but not delete) and `C:\Users\Public` are such directories. advisories.title: filelock: On Windows an oplock on a soft lock's marker holds SoftFileLock.acquire() past its timeout and blocks the stale break
advisories.summary: On Windows the soft locks (`SoftFileLock`, `MarkerSoftFileLock`, `SoftFileLease`, their async forms, and a `FileLock` that fell back to a soft lock) read their marker by path. The marker is the lock file whose presence says a process holds the lock. Each `acquire()` attempt that finds a marker opens it with `os.open` to read the holder's process id, and the lock renames and deletes a marker it judges stale, by path. On Windows each of these calls waits for an oplock. An oplock (opportunistic lock) is a request by a process that holds a handle on a file to be told before another process opens, renames or deletes that file; the other process waits until the holder answers the break or closes its handle. Another local account that can open the marker for reading can take a Level 1 oplock on it while no process holds it open, and leave the break unanswered. Every `acquire()` by the user running the lock (below: the lock user) then waits inside the open, past its `timeout`, `blocking=False` and `cancel_check`, and a stale marker under that oplock is not broken. Mutual exclusion holds and the lock touches no other file. Affected versions are filelock 3.22.0 through 4.2.0 on Windows. advisories.title: DSA-6581-1 unbound - security update
advisories.summary:
Multiple security vulnerabilities were discovered in Unbound, a validating, recursive, caching DNS resolver.

CVE-2026-35501

(DNSSEC) Bypass of a configured island trust anchor underneath an insecure parent from an attacker-controlled NSEC record.

CVE-2026-50106

(DNSSEC) Possible insecure NXDOMAIN for non-existing records under a configured island trust anchor underneath an insecure parent.

CVE-2026-96405

Aggregate DNS name chained pointer decompression work leads to degradation of service.

CVE-2026-97206

DNS-over-QUIC path-migration can lead to use-after-free on multi-threaded deployments, leading to potential denial of service.

CVE-2026-109125

Possible cache poisoning vulnerability via a cache side-channel exposed by 'unwanted-reply-threshold'.

https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/DSA-6581-1

advisories.summary: Traefik v3.7.13 before v3.7.14 contains an access-control bypass in the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider, where the HTTP router generated for ssl-passthrough Ingresses on non-TLS entry points never applies the Ingress's access-control annotations. advisories.title: Javo Spot theme for WordPress before 3.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files via the fn parameter of the jv
advisories.summary: Javo Spot theme for WordPress before 3.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files via the fn parameter of the jvfrm_spot_get_json AJAX action. Attackers can send GET requests to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php with fn set to ../../wp-config.php to retrieve database credentials and secret keys. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

advisories.summary: Intermesh Group-Office 3.3.0 before 3.5.5 contains an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in compress.php that allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files by manipulating the 'file' parameter. Attackers can send GET requests to /compress.php with '../' sequences in the 'file' parameter, which is appended to the cache path and passed to readfile(), to read files such as /etc/passwd. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-21.

advisories.title: Malicious code in event-emitter-testmetest (npm)
advisories.summary: event-emitter-testmetest was published by npm account `testnewtestme2` on 2026-10-21, first to test the delivery chain of data-pipeline-testmetest 2.0.1 and then to ship it. 1.0.6 and 1.0.7 ship an obfuscated `index.js` loader that decrypts a filler stage and pipes it into Bun with the full environment: 1.0.6 runs it on load, 1.0.7 on `npm install` via a `binding.gyp` source `<!(env node index.js >/dev/null 2>&1; echo stub.c)`. 4.1.0 and 5.0.0 ship rebuilds of the full stealer behind the same `binding.gyp` hook: inline in `index.js` in 4.1.0, and in an encrypted `data.bin` that `index.js` decrypts in 5.0.0. Other versions carry no executable payload. --- Credit: [OpenSSF](https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages) ([source](https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages/blob/d00528d10daab38eadcbc9a9c17890a17aa25e95/osv/malicious/npm/event-emitter-testmetest/MAL-2026-18178.json))

advisories.title: RCE via OOM corruption
advisories.summary: ## Summary PHP uses `longjmp()` for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. In some contexts, request memory is temporarily reachable before it is fully initialized. If any allocation fails at that point, PHP does not properly account for the early exit and leaves the request memory in an invalid state. The failed allocation does not need to be related to the invalid memory. The request shutdown procedure may then read or branch on it. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE). ## Vulnerability ### OOM strategies Several multipart parsing problems can let a request reach OOM while remaining within its apparent PHP limits: - A multipart request without a usable declared content length may pass the initial `post_max_size` check and continue supplying decoded body data. - A multipart part can contain an unrestricted number of headers. Representing these headers inside PHP can use substantially more memory than their wire representation, allowing a request within `post_max_size` to exhaust the normal `memory_limit`. - Empty file controls do not count towards `max_file_uploads` but still create the normal file metadata arrays. advisories.title: RCE via stale global state
advisories.summary: ## Summary PHP contains various global state, such as error, session, object and extension state that is retained by a worker but points to memory owned by one request. That state must be reset before the request memory is released. Some input, configuration, session and error handling operations run before normal initialization of the next request. They inadvertently access stale state not reset by the previous request before initialization has a chance to replace it, causing a use after free. A strategically crafted heap layout can produce full remote code execution (RCE). State can survive for more than one reason. A fatal error, including one caused by memory exhaustion, can abandon an operation before it performs its matching reset. A warning or other nonfatal diagnostic can also repopulate error state after that state was already cleared during shutdown. The request heap is then freed while the worker global field still refers to it. A later operation that runs before normal request initialization can consume the stale value. advisories.title: toml-node is a TOML parser for Node.js and the browser
advisories.summary: toml-node is a TOML parser for Node.js and the browser. Prior to 5.0.1, toml.parse() repeatedly slices and rejoins every path prefix in lib/compiler.js while processing long dotted keys, table headers, array-of-tables headers, and inline-table keys in assign(), deepRef(), and setNestedKey(). The resulting quadratic work can block the Node.js event loop for several seconds, and sufficiently long paths can terminate the process through memory exhaustion. The maxDepth option does not limit key-segment count and therefore does not mitigate this path. This issue is fixed in version 5.0.1.

advisories.title: Pillow is a Python imaging library
advisories.summary: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 5.1.0 until 13.0.0, PdfParser.linearize_page_tree() in src/PIL/PdfParser.py treats a PDF /Pages graph as a tree without tracking duplicate indirect references. When Image.save(..., format="PDF", append=True) processes an attacker-controlled existing PDF whose /Kids arrays repeatedly reference the same child /Pages node, Pillow expands the shared subtree as distinct pages. A compact malformed PDF can therefore create exponentially many page references and consume disproportionate CPU before the append completes. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

advisories.title: Pillow is a Python imaging library
advisories.summary: Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, PILfont text-width accumulation in src/_imaging.c checks positive glyph advances against INT_MAX but does not check negative advances against INT_MIN. Repeating a signed 16-bit advance of -32768 can therefore execute a signed C integer overflow in xsize += dx, producing a large positive width from a negative mathematical result. Applications that use getlength(), getsize(), or derived layout, quota, serialization, or allocation calculations can experience logic-integrity errors or resource consumption, while the high-level mask path commonly retains a decompression-bomb check. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

From 9.4.0 until 13.0.0, ImagingJpegEncode() in src/libImaging/JpegEncode.c can call jpeg_write_marker() for a JPEG COM comment when an ICC profile has exactly filled the 65536-byte encoder buffer. libjpeg writes one byte before checking the exhausted free_in_buffer counter, which then wraps and permits the attacker-controlled comment and subsequent compressed image data to overwrite adjacent heap memory. Re-saving an untrusted image as JPEG while preserving its ICC profile and forwarded comment can crash the process and may enable code execution in suitable runtime and heap layouts. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

advisories.title: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js
advisories.summary: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From 3.13.0 until 4.6.2, the server-island renderer serializes raw useHeadSafe entry input into the island response without preserving the safe-input marker, and NuxtIsland later inserts that input into the page head as an ordinary entry. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.2 .

advisories.title: Django REST framework is a toolkit for building Web APIs
advisories.summary: Django REST framework is a toolkit for building Web APIs. Prior to 3.18.2, DefaultContentNegotiation.get_accept_list in rest_framework/negotiation.py accepts an unbounded number and aggregate size of Accept tokens, while select_renderer in that file repeatedly invokes _MediaType parsing from rest_framework/utils/mediatypes.py for each attacker-controlled token, every renderer, and forced 406 renegotiation. A remote unauthenticated client can send many distinct media types containing large quoted parameter values with numerous semicolons, causing Django's parameter parser and DRF's repeated parsing structure to consume disproportionate CPU. Requests to any reachable endpoint can pin synchronous workers for prolonged periods, and concurrent requests can make the service unavailable until the requests stop. This issue is fixed in version 3.18.2.

advisories.summary: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 9.1.0 until 13.0.0, BmpRleDecoder.decode() in src/PIL/BmpImagePlugin.py permits crafted RLE BMP delta escapes and absolute-mode runs to append beyond the remaining dest_length without a per-branch cap. A delta can add roughly 255 image rows in one iteration, so a kilobyte-sized file with a large but permitted width can expand the data bytearray to hundreds of megabytes or more, causing memory-exhaustion denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

advisories.title: Pillow is a Python imaging library
advisories.summary: Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0 on Windows, src/PIL/WmfImagePlugin.py passes unchecked 32-bit WMF or EMF dimensions to the native drawwmf handler in src/display.c. The handler sizes a DIB allocation from 16-bit-truncated bcWidth and bcHeight fields but copies pixel data using the original full dimensions. A crafted wide, short metafile can pass the pixel-count decompression-bomb check and make the Windows-only renderer read beyond the heap buffer, potentially disclosing memory or crashing the process. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

advisories.summary: Argo CD is a declarative, GitOps continuous delivery tool for Kubernetes. Although generated Secrets are redacted, placing imported contents in a ConfigMap returns the data to the caller. Using importstr on a non-terminating device such as /dev/zero can exhaust repo-server memory. advisories.title: virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments
advisories.summary: virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.13.0, the bash activate script that zsh also sources leaves the environment name unescaped; from 21.13.0 until 21.14.4, it escapes backslashes, dollar signs, and backticks only when BASH_VERSION is set, so zsh receives the raw value. The script assigns that value to PS1. In zsh with PROMPT_SUBST, an attacker-influenced environment directory, --prompt, or VIRTUALENV_PROMPT value containing command, parameter, or arithmetic expansion syntax can therefore execute commands in the user's shell each time the prompt is drawn. A percent sign is separately interpreted as a zsh prompt escape but does not by itself execute commands. Plain zsh with PROMPT_SUBST disabled and bash are not affected by this mechanism. This issue is fixed in version 21.14.4.

advisories.title: CVE-2026-105007 Windows NDIS Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
advisories.summary: An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in the Network Driver Interface Specification (NDIS) when ndis.sys fails to check the length of a buffer prior to copying memory to it. To exploit the vulnerability, in a local attack scenario, an attacker could run a specially crafted application to elevate the attacker's privilege level. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could run processes in an elevated context. However, an attacker must first gain access to the local system with the ability to execute a malicious application in order to exploit this vulnerability. The security update addresses the vulnerability by changing how ndis.sys validates buffer length.

advisories.title: .NET SocketAsyncEventArgs memory corruption remote code execution
advisories.summary: On Windows, reusing SocketAsyncEventArgs across IPv4 and IPv6 datagram sockets can retain an undersized native address buffer. Untrusted datagrams can trigger an out of bounds memory write. The original October 13 fix was incomplete; Microsoft provided corrected patches October 25.
advisories.affected: Affected .NET 8 prior to 8.0.33, .NET 9 before 9.0.22, .NET 10 before 10.0.14, and affected .NET 11 previews before RC3 on Windows when the vulnerable socket behavior is reachable.
advisories.remediation: Update affected installations to .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22 or 10.0.14 (or .NET 11 RC3 for prerelease installations). Rebuild self-contained apps and containers with the fixed runtimes, and update affected NuGet packages where the advisory requires it. The October 13 releases alone do not fully fix this CVE.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed active exploitation stated in the cited Microsoft security advisory.
advisories.status: Vendor-sourced historical baseline; not newly disclosed
advisories.action: Verify the affected version and exposure, then follow the vendor remediation.

advisories.title: ASP.NET Core Blazor WebAssembly debugger code execution
advisories.summary: The Blazor WebAssembly debug proxy may compile attacker-influenced debugger expressions into C# without sufficient escaping, enabling code execution on a developer workstation when a developer evaluates affected data. Microsoft corrected an incomplete October 13 package fix on October 25.
advisories.affected: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server and Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.DevServer 10.x before 10.0.14 and affected .NET 11 prereleases before 11.0.0 RC3. This requires vulnerable debugging activity and is not a general production request endpoint issue.
advisories.remediation: Update both affected Blazor WebAssembly Server and DevServer NuGet packages to 10.0.14 or 11.0.0 RC3 as applicable, and update the development SDK. A shared runtime update alone does not fix independently referenced packages.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed active exploitation stated in the cited Microsoft advisory.

advisories.title: ASP.NET Core HTTP/2 Kestrel request desynchronization
advisories.summary: Kestrel accepts newline characters in HTTP/2 trailers or dynamic HPACK table values when it should reject malformed headers, allowing potential HTTP request desynchronization and a security feature bypass.
advisories.affected: Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime versions 8.0.0 through 8.0.31, 9.0.0 through 9.0.20, 10.0.0 through 10.0.12, and .NET 11 prereleases through RC1.
advisories.remediation: Fixed initially in ASP.NET Core 8.0.32, 9.0.21, 10.0.13 and .NET 11 RC2. Install the newer supported October 25 releases where applicable (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14, RC3).
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed exploitation in the cited Microsoft advisory.

advisories.title: ASP.NET Core Kestrel HTTP/1 request smuggling
advisories.summary: An aborted Kestrel HTTP/1 connection can cause unread request body data to be reparsed as a new request, allowing HTTP request smuggling or message desynchronization in affected ASP.NET Core hosts.
advisories.affected: Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime versions 8.0.0 through 8.0.31, 9.0.0 through 9.0.20, 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and corresponding affected .NET 11 prereleases.

advisories.exploitation: No confirmed exploitation in the cited Microsoft advisory.

advisories.title: .NET Framework untrusted search path security feature bypass
advisories.summary: Untrusted search path handling in classic Microsoft .NET Framework permits a locally authorized attacker to bypass a security feature. The patch is part of Microsoft's October 2026 .NET Framework cumulative security updates.
advisories.affected: Multiple .NET Framework 3.5, 4.6.2 through 4.8.1 configurations across supported Windows versions, subject to Microsoft update applicability. This is a separate classic .NET Framework CVE, not the modern .NET Brotli issue.
advisories.remediation: Install the correct October 13, 2026 .NET Framework cumulative update or a newer superseding Windows update for the installed Windows and .NET Framework versions. Consult the Microsoft patch matrix for the specific KB.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed active exploitation in the referenced Microsoft advisories.

advisories.title: The FV Player 8 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 8.1.7 via the check_mimetype function
advisories.summary: The FV Player 8 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 8.1.7 via the check_mimetype function. This is due to insufficient file type validation in check_mimetype(), which writes attacker-supplied remote file content to the public uploads directory before any MIME or extension check, combined with a missing capability check on new player creation. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. This requires successfully exploiting a race condition, and is only exploitable if the '[fvplayer_editor]' shortcode is present, or the "Enable profile videos" setting is enabled.

advisories.title: Improper state management in MongoDB libmongocrypt can cause provider-specific data to be treated as an incompatible type when cleaning up a key document containing duplicate
advisories.summary: Improper state management in MongoDB libmongocrypt can cause provider-specific data to be treated as an incompatible type when cleaning up a key document containing duplicate masterKey fields. An authenticated actor who can modify key vault documents, or a server that returns such a key document, can cause invalid memory access and invalid frees in the client process. This can terminate the application or corrupt process memory.

advisories.title: The BSON buffer-reservation API in the MongoDB C Driver can record a length smaller than the five-byte BSON minimum
advisories.summary: The BSON buffer-reservation API in the MongoDB C Driver can record a length smaller than the five-byte BSON minimum. Later append or comparison operations can underflow unsigned length calculations and read or write outside the document buffer. An actor who can influence the length supplied by an embedding application can cause the application to terminate or read or corrupt adjacent process memory. Reaching this issue requires the application to pass an undersized value to bson_reserve_buffer and then perform an affected operation.

Fix this by making sure the buffer has room for at least 8 bytes and that those 8 bytes are pre-cleared. advisories.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: pcm: Serialize PCM mmap with buffer reallocation to fix page UAF snd_pcm_hw_params() and snd_pcm_hw_free() guard buffer reallocation with an mmap_count check performed under the PCM stream lock, but the lock is released long before the buffer is actually freed: snd_pcm_sync_stop(), constraint refinement and do_free_pages() all happen in between. snd_pcm_mmap_data(), on the other hand, takes no lock at all: it validates against the old buffer's state and dma_bytes, remaps its pages into the VMA, and only then increments mmap_count. A concurrent mmap() can therefore slip in between the check and the free. remap_pfn_range() installs writable PTEs for the old buffer's pages without taking page references, and the subsequent do_free_pages() returns those pages to the page allocator while the VMA still maps them. This leaves a stale, writable mapping of freed pages: a page-level use-after-free that can be leveraged for local privilege escalation. Make snd_pcm_mmap_data() participate in the buffer-access scheme introduced for hw_params/hw_free: acquire runtime->buffer_accessing before validating and remapping, and release it afterwards. advisories.title: IPv6 ACL bypass in FastCGI listen.allowed_clients due to partial address comparison (memcmp 12 bytes)
advisories.summary: ### Summary The IPv6 branch of the FastCGI client access check compares only the first 12 bytes of a 16-byte IPv6 address, so `listen.allowed_clients` matches on a /96 prefix instead of the exact address. An attacker who can source an address sharing the first 96 bits with an allowed one passes the check and reaches the FastCGI endpoint. ### Details `fcgi_is_allowed()` in `main/fastcgi.c` compares IPv6 client addresses with a hard-coded length of 12: https://github.com/php/php-src/blob/php-8.5.10/main/fastcgi.c#L1334 An exact IPv6 comparison must cover all 16 bytes of `struct in6_addr`. The IPv4 branch above it compares its full 4 bytes correctly, and the `IN6_IS_ADDR_V4MAPPED` branch legitimately uses a 12-byte offset to reach the embedded IPv4 address, but that offset is not a valid length for a plain IPv6 comparison. Allowed addresses are parsed as full addresses with `inet_pton(AF_INET6, ...)`, so the truncated comparison silently widens every configured entry to a /96 network. The fix compares `sizeof(client_sa.sa_inet6.sin6_addr)` bytes. ### PoC Tested against a real `php-fpm` (fpm-fcgi), not a mock. 1. advisories.title: CVE-2026-76654
advisories.summary: CVSS Rating: [CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N) - Medium (5.8) An NTLM coercion vulnerability exists on Windows nodes when the subPath supplied in a pod's volumeMounts is set to a symbolic link that points to an attacker-controlled network share. When a kubelet resolves symlinks, it does not reject a target that resolves to a UNC path. As a result, the kubelet will transparently attempt to authenticate to the share using NTLM. This allows an attacker to obtain the NetNTLMv2 hash of the account under which the kubelet is running. An attacker could then attempt to crack the hash to retrieve the corresponding password or relay it to impersonate the node, if the node is domain-joined. #### Affected Versions kubelet: <= v1.34.11 kubelet: <= v1.35.8 kubelet: <= v1.36.4 kubelet: = v1.37.0 ### How do I mitigate this vulnerability? This issue can be mitigated by upgrading to a fixed kubelet version. The fixed versions update kubelet to refuse UNC symlink targets on Windows. #### Fixed Versions

advisories.title: Froxlor before 2.2.0 (affected up to and including 2.2.0-rc3) generates /etc/pure-ftpd/db/mysql.conf with mode 0644 via the XML configuration templates in lib/configfiles/, ev
advisories.summary: Froxlor before 2.2.0 (affected up to and including 2.2.0-rc3) generates /etc/pure-ftpd/db/mysql.conf with mode 0644 via the XML configuration templates in lib/configfiles/, even though the file contains the Froxlor SQL user's password. On systems where the parent directories are world readable (the default on Debian 12), any unprivileged local user able to execute commands or code on the host — including virtual users without SSH access who can upload PHP/CGI scripts — can read the file and obtain the Froxlor database credentials. Database access can then be leveraged to alter an administrator's password hash and TOTP seed, log in as a Froxlor administrator, and ultimately gain root privileges. Only instances configured to use pure-ftpd are affected.

advisories.title: langgraph-api: Incomplete assistant authorization in LangGraph Server run creation
advisories.summary: ## Summary In affected versions of `langgraph-api` (the LangGraph Server runtime), the run-creation path authorized the assistant attached to a run using a different authorization event than the rest of the assistant-handling code paths. Direct assistant reads and cron creation dispatch the `assistants.read` authorization event; run creation dispatched `assistants.search` with an incomplete value. In deployments whose custom authorization handlers register only an `assistants.read` handler (without an `assistants.search` handler and without a global fallback handler), no handler was consulted on the run-creation path, the returned filter set was empty, and the owner constraint was omitted from the resulting query. As a result, in those deployments a request to create a run could reference a private assistant owned by another user, even where direct assistant reads, assistant search, and cron creation against that assistant were correctly denied. The run-creation response merged the referenced assistant's `metadata`, `config`, and `context` into fields returned to the requesting user. advisories.title: langgraph-api: Relative webhook targets in LangGraph Server can reach in-process routes without authentication
advisories.summary: ## Summary In affected versions of `langgraph-api` (the LangGraph Server runtime), a run or cron could be created with a relative webhook target. When the server later delivers such a webhook, it routes the request back into the same application through an in-process loopback transport that the authentication middleware treats as internal and does not authenticate. As a result, a relative webhook target could reach the server's own routes that operate on threads and runs without the authentication context that applies to ordinary external requests. In deployments that scope threads and runs by owner, this could allow a request associated with one user to reach routes operating on another user's thread, resulting in creation of a run on (or modification of the state of) a thread owned by another user, even where the corresponding direct external requests were correctly denied. Limited metadata from the targeted thread may be incorporated into the created run record. We have no evidence of this behavior occurring in the wild. ## Affected users / systems You may be affected if you: - run `langgraph-api` (the LangGraph Server / Agent Server runtime, including via the LangGraph Platform Helm chart), - allow runs or crons to specify webhook targets, and - rely on per-user authorization

advisories.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: i2c: davinci: fix division by zero on missing clock-frequency When the 'clock-frequency' property is missin
advisories.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: i2c: davinci: fix division by zero on missing clock-frequency When the 'clock-frequency' property is missing from the device tree, the driver falls back to DAVINCI_I2C_DEFAULT_BUS_FREQ. However, this macro was defined in kHz (100), whereas the device tree property is expected in Hz. The probe function divided the fallback value by 1000, causing integer truncation that resulted in dev->bus_freq = 0. This triggered a deterministic division-by-zero kernel panic when calculating clock dividers later in the probe sequence. Fix this by redefining DAVINCI_I2C_DEFAULT_BUS_FREQ in Hz (100000) to match the expected device tree property unit, allowing the existing division logic to work correctly for both cases.

advisories.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/damon/sysfs-schemes: delete tried region in regions_rmdirs() DAMON sysfs maintains the DAMOS tried regio
advisories.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/damon/sysfs-schemes: delete tried region in regions_rmdirs() DAMON sysfs maintains the DAMOS tried region directory objects via a linked list. When the user requests refresh of the directories, DAMON sysfs removes all the region directories first, and then generate updated regions directory on the empty space. The removal function (damon_sysfs_scheme_regions_rm_dirs()) only puts the kobj objects. Deletion of the container region object from the linked list is done inside the kobj release callback function. If somehow the callback invocation is delayed, the list will contain regions list that gonna be freed. If the updated region directories creation is started in this situation, the list can be corrupted and use-after-free can happen. Because the kobj objects are managed by only DAMON sysfs, the issue cannot happen in normal situation. But, such delays can be made on kernels that built with CONFIG_DEBUG_KOBJECT_RELEASE. On the kernel, the issue can indeed be reproduced like below. # damo start --damos_action stat # cd /sys/kernel/mm/damon/admin/kdamonds/0/ # for i in {1..10}; do echo update_schemes_tried_regions > state; done # dmesg | grep underflow [ 89.29615

advisories.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Bluetooth: HIDP: fix missing length checks in hidp_input_report() hidp_input_report() reads keyboard and mo
advisories.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Bluetooth: HIDP: fix missing length checks in hidp_input_report() hidp_input_report() reads keyboard and mouse payload data from an skb without first verifying that skb->len contains enough data. hidp_recv_intr_frame() pulls the 1-byte HIDP header before dispatching to hidp_input_report(). If a paired device sends a truncated packet, the handler reads beyond the valid skb data, resulting in an out-of-bounds read of skb data. The OOB bytes may be interpreted as phantom key presses or spurious mouse movement. Replace the open-coded length tracking and pointer arithmetic with skb_pull_data() calls. skb_pull_data() returns NULL if the requested bytes are not present, eliminating the need for a manual size variable and the separate skb->len guard.

advisories.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: SEV: Compute the correct max length of the in-GHCB scratch area When setting the length of the GHCB sc
advisories.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: SEV: Compute the correct max length of the in-GHCB scratch area When setting the length of the GHCB scratch area, and the area is in the GHCB shared buffer, set the effective length of the scratch area to the max possible size given the start of the guest-provided pointer, and the end of the shared buffer. The code was "fine" when first introduced, as KVM doesn't consult the length of the buffer when emulating MMIO, because the passed in @len always specifies the *max* size required. But for PSC requests, the incoming @len is just the minimum length (to process the header), and KVM needs to know the full size of the scratch area to avoid buffer overflows (spoiler alert). Opportunistically rename @len => @min_len to better reflect its role.

advisories.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Bluetooth: ISO: fix UAF in iso_recv_frame iso_recv_frame reads conn->sk under iso_conn_lock but releases th
advisories.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Bluetooth: ISO: fix UAF in iso_recv_frame iso_recv_frame reads conn->sk under iso_conn_lock but releases the lock before using sk, with no reference held. A concurrent iso_sock_kill() can free sk in that window, causing use-after-free on sk->sk_state and sock_queue_rcv_skb(). Fix by replacing the bare pointer read with iso_sock_hold(conn), which calls sock_hold() while the spinlock is held, atomically elevating the refcount before the lock drops. Add a drop_put label so sock_put() is called on all exit paths where the hold succeeded.

advisories.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: memfd: deny writeable mappings when implying SEAL_WRITE When SEAL_EXEC is added, SEAL_WRITE is implied to m
advisories.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: memfd: deny writeable mappings when implying SEAL_WRITE When SEAL_EXEC is added, SEAL_WRITE is implied to make W^X. But the implied seal is set after the check that makes sure the memfd can not have any writable mappings. This means one can use SEAL_EXEC to apply SEAL_WRITE while having writeable mappings. This breaks the contract that SEAL_WRITE provides and can be used by an attacker to pass a memfd that appears to be write sealed but can still be modified arbitrarily. Fix this by adding the implied seals before the call for mapping_deny_writable() is done.

advisories.title: The Image Optimizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion in versions up to and including 1.7.4
advisories.summary: The Image Optimizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion in versions up to and including 1.7.4. This is due to insufficient path validation in the Image_Backup::remove() function where backup file paths stored in post meta are used directly in file deletion operations without verifying they are within the uploads directory. The plugin stores backup file paths in the image_optimizer_metadata post meta field and trusts these paths completely when deleting backups on the delete_attachment hook. An authenticated attacker with Author-level access can edit the image_optimizer_metadata post meta on their own attachments via WordPress's Custom Fields interface, injecting arbitrary absolute file paths into the backups array. When the attacker subsequently deletes the attachment, the plugin calls File_System::delete() on each path without validation. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Author-level access and above, to delete arbitrary files on the server within the web server's filesystem permissions, potentially leading to denial of service, data loss, or security degradation.

advisories.summary: ## Summary In `backpropagate >= 1.1.0`, the optional Reflex web UI (`pip install backpropagate[ui]`, launched via `backprop ui`) exposes a training control plane: dataset upload, model load, training start/stop, multi-run orchestration, GGUF export, and HuggingFace Hub push. The CLI accepts two operator-facing flags intended as security controls: - `--auth user:pass` — documented as "require HTTP Basic authentication on every request to the UI." - `--share` — documented as "expose the UI on a public address; requires `--auth`." When `--auth user:pass` is passed, the CLI prints `Auth: enabled (user: <username>)` to confirm to the operator that authentication is active, then exports `BACKPROPAGATE_UI_AUTH=user:pass` to the subprocess that launches the Reflex backend. **The Reflex backend (`backpropagate/ui_app/**`) never reads `BACKPROPAGATE_UI_AUTH`.** No authentication middleware is registered. advisories.title: LiquidJS has a memory and render limit bypass via unbounded width padding in `date` filter (strftime)
advisories.summary: ## Summary The `date` filter's strftime implementation parses width specifiers like `%9999999d` and forwards the captured width unchecked into `pad()`/`padStart()` in `src/util/underscore.ts`. The pad loop performs unbounded string concatenation without consulting the Context's `memoryLimit` or `renderLimit`, so a single small template (`{{ x | date: '%5000000d' }}`) produces megabytes of output and unbounded CPU. The `memoryLimit` and `renderLimit` options the docs (`src/liquid-options.ts:87-92`) advertise as DoS controls — and which the docstring explicitly mentions for `strftime` — are entirely bypassed. ## Details `date.ts:5-13` only charges `memoryLimit` for the lengths of the input value, format string, and timezone: ```ts export function date (this: FilterImpl, v: string | Date, format?: string, timezoneOffset?: number | string) { const size = ((v as string)?.length ?? 0) + (format?.length ?? 0) + ((timezoneOffset as string)?.length ?? 0) this.context.memoryLimit.use(size) ... return strftime(date, format) } ``` `strftime` (`src/util/strftime.ts:121`) then walks the format with `rFormat = /%([-_0^#:]+)?(\d+)?([EO])?(.)/`. The captured `width` group is passed directly to `padStart`: ```ts function format (d, match) { const [input, flagStr = '', width, modifier, conversion]
advisories.affected: npm: liquidjs (<= 10.25.7)
advisories.remediation: liquidjs: 10.26.0

advisories.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: skbuff: preserve shared-frag marker during coalescing skb_try_coalesce() can attach paged frags from @
advisories.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: skbuff: preserve shared-frag marker during coalescing skb_try_coalesce() can attach paged frags from @from to @to. If @from has SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG set, the resulting @to skb can contain the same externally-owned or page-cache-backed frags, but the shared-frag marker is currently lost. That breaks the invariant relied on by later in-place writers. In particular, ESP input checks skb_has_shared_frag() before deciding whether an uncloned nonlinear skb can skip skb_cow_data(). If TCP receive coalescing has moved shared frags into an unmarked skb, ESP can see skb_has_shared_frag() as false and decrypt in place over page-cache backed frags. Propagate SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG when skb_try_coalesce() transfers paged frags. The tailroom copy path does not need the marker because it copies bytes into @to's linear data rather than transferring frag descriptors.

advisories.title: imgaug contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in BackgroundAugmenter class within multicore.py module
advisories.summary: The imgaug library thru 0.4.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in its BackgroundAugmenter class within the multicore.py module. The class uses Python's pickle module to deserialize data received via a multiprocessing queue in the _augment_images_worker() method without any safety checks. An attacker who can influence the data placed into this queue (e.g., through social engineering, malicious input scripts, or a compromised shared queue) can provide a malicious pickle payload. When deserialized, this payload can execute arbitrary code in the context of the worker process, leading to remote or local code execution depending on the deployment scenario.

advisories.title: Guardrails AI contains a code injection vulnerability in its Hub package installation mechanism
advisories.summary: Guardrails AI thru 0.6.7 contains a code injection vulnerability (CWE-94) in its Hub package installation mechanism. When installing validator packages via guardrails hub install, the system retrieves a manifest from the Guardrails Hub and dynamically executes a script specified in the post_install field. The script path is constructed from untrusted manifest data and executed without proper validation or sanitization, allowing remote code execution. An attacker who can publish malicious packages to the Hub can inject arbitrary code that will be executed on any system where a victim installs the malicious package.

advisories.title: Horovod contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in its KVStore HTTP server component
advisories.summary: Horovod thru 0.28.1 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability (CWE-502) in its KVStore HTTP server component. The KVStore server, used for distributed task coordination, lacks authentication and authorization controls, allowing any remote attacker to write arbitrary data via HTTP PUT requests. When a Horovod worker reads data from the KVStore (via HTTP GET), it deserializes the data using cloudpickle.loads() without verifying its source or integrity. An attacker can exploit this by sending a malicious pickle payload to the server before the legitimate data is written, causing the victim worker to deserialize and execute arbitrary code, leading to remote code execution.

advisories.title: Wallos is an open-source, self-hostable personal subscription tracker
advisories.summary: Wallos is an open-source, self-hostable personal subscription tracker. Prior to version 4.8.1, the SSRF protection in endpoints/subscription/add.php (line 42) and endpoints/payments/add.php (line 40) uses an inline IP validation check (FILTER_FLAG_NO_PRIV_RANGE | FILTER_FLAG_NO_RES_RANGE) that does not block CGNAT addresses (100.64.0.0/10, RFC 6598). The includes/ssrf_helper.php file explicitly defines is_cgnat_ip() to cover this gap (used by notification endpoints), but the logo/icon URL fetching in subscription and payment endpoints performs its own inline validation that misses this range. This allows authenticated users to perform Blind SSRF to internal services in Tailscale, Carrier-Grade NAT, and other environments using 100.64.0.0/10 addresses. This issue has been patched in version 4.8.1.

advisories.title: PhpSpreadsheet is a pure PHP library for reading and writing spreadsheet files
advisories.summary: PhpSpreadsheet is a pure PHP library for reading and writing spreadsheet files. The HTML writer skips htmlspecialchars escaping when a cell's formatted value differs from the original value. When a cell has a custom number format containing the text placeholder @ along with any additional literal characters (for example ". @", "@ ", or "x@"), the formatter replaces @ with the cell value and adds the extra characters, causing the formatted value to differ from the original and bypassing HTML escaping entirely. An attacker who can control the cell value and number format of an uploaded spreadsheet that is later converted to HTML and displayed to other users can achieve stored cross-site scripting. This issue is fixed in versions 5.7.0, 3.10.5, 2.4.5, 2.1.16, and 1.30.4.

Use auto-generated filenames only 3. Implement strict input validation if `name` must be used ```python from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename import os # Sanitize user input before passing to save() safe_name = secure_filename(request.form.get('custom_name')) # Remove path separators safe_name = os.path.basename(safe_name) # Validate extension matches policy if not photos.extension_allowed(photos.get_extension(safe_name)): abort(400) filename = photos.save(file, name=safe_name) ``` ### Resources The fix is documented in the pull request, see https://github.com/jugmac00/flask-reuploaded/pull/180. A proper write-up was created by the reporter of the vulnerability, Jaron Cabral (https://www.linkedin.com/in/jaron-cabral-751994357/), but is not yet available as of time of this publication.

advisories.title: EPyT-Flow vulnerable to unsafe JSON deserialization (__type__)
advisories.summary: ### Impact EPyT-Flow’s REST API parses attacker-controlled JSON request bodies using a custom deserializer (my_load_from_json) that supports a __type__ field. When __type__ is present, the deserializer dynamically imports an attacker-specified module/class and instantiates it with attacker-supplied arguments. This allows invoking dangerous classes such as subprocess.Popen, which can lead to OS command execution during JSON parsing. This also affects the loading of JSON files. ### Patches EPyT-Flow has been patched in 0.16.1 -- affects all versions <= 0.16.0 ### Workarounds Do not load any JSON from untrusted sources and do not expose the REST API. ### Credits EPyT-Flow thanks Jarrett Chan (@syphonetic) for detecting and reporting the bug.

advisories.title: dcap-qvl has Missing Verification for QE Identity
advisories.summary: ## Impact This vulnerability involves a critical gap in the cryptographic verification process within the dcap-qvl. The library fetches QE Identity collateral (including qe_identity, qe_identity_signature, and qe_identity_issuer_chain) from the PCCS. However, it skips to verify the QE Identity signature against its certificate chain and does not enforce policy constraints on the QE Report. ## Consequences An attacker can forge the QE Identity data to whitelist a malicious or non-Intel Quoting Enclave. This allows the attacker to forge the QE and sign untrusted quotes that the verifier will accept as valid. Effectively, this bypasses the entire remote attestation security model, as the verifier can no longer trust the entity responsible for signing the quotes. ## Who is impacted All deployments utilizing the dcap-qvl library for SGX or TDX quote verification are affected. ## Patches The vulnerability has been patched in dcap-qvl version 0.3.9. The fix implements the missing cryptographic verification for the QE Identity signature and enforces the required checks for MRSIGNER, ISVPRODID, and ISVSVN against the QE Report. Users of the `@phala/dcap-qvl-node` and `@phala/dcap-qvl-web` packages should switch to the pure JavaScript implementation, `@phala/dcap-qvl`. ## Workarounds There
